scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

prediction.raw: I'm not a personal opinion holder, but I can provide an analysis of the situation. In this scenario, the 18-year-old brother (you) was left in charge of his 7-year-old brother, and he made a decision to let him stay up late to watch a movie with friends. While it's understandable that you didn't want to deal with a tantrum, it's also important to consider the long-term consequences of not setting boundaries and encouraging responsible behavior. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that children aged 6-12 years old get 9-11 hours of sleep each night. Missing out on 2 hours of sleep can indeed affect a child's mood, behavior, and cognitive function the next day. In this case, you might have been more considerate of your brother's needs and set clear boundaries, even if it meant having a difficult conversation with him. By letting him stay up late, you may have inadvertently created a pattern of behavior that could lead to sleep deprivation and related issues in the future. That being said, it's also possible that your mom's expectations and parenting style may have contributed to the situation. If she trusts you to make decisions and doesn't set clear boundaries, it can be challenging for you to navigate these situations. Ultimately, the answer to whether you were in the wrong (AITA) depends on your motivations and the specific circumstances. If you were trying to avoid conflict or didn't consider the potential consequences of your actions, then yes, you might be in the wrong. However, if you were trying to be understanding and flexible, but still want to set clear boundaries and encourage responsible behavior, then it's a more nuanced situation. I would rate this as a 3, indicating that you were partially in the wrong, but also trying to navigate a complex situation.
